author: Claude Code
no_provider_calls: Nothing in this wave has been submitted to Meshy or ElevenLabs and no credits have been spent. The coordinator launches jobs only after validate_requests.py passes and the PO approves the credit estimate.
selection_rationale: Three new style-library anchors, each in an SFX group not yet in production, so no request overlaps the in-flight Skyline Seer work (AI-050/051/053, group ZEUS_HUMAN). Silhouettes are deliberately different: a low quadruped wedge (Zeus), a tall limbless coil (Poseidon), and a wide squat ring-in-arch structure (board). Each one anchors a shared SFX group that covers 10, 3, and 4 cards.

source.name: Thunder Ram
source.description: A storm front taught to break walls.

requests.silhouette_notes: Wide, low, horn-led body on four planted legs. Reads nothing like the upright staff-bearing Skyline Seer. 'Ram' is interpreted as a war ram beast because the card is a SIEGE character, not a battering-ram object.

meshy.prompt: Stylized 3D game miniature for a hex-tile tactics board game: Thunder Ram, an original Zeus-faction siege beast. A four-legged war ram of bronze armor over dark marble, head lowered to charge, massive forward-curled horns wrapped in gold-white lightning, storm-cloud mane along its spine. Silhouette: wide low wedge body, heavy horns leading, four thick legs planted square. Regal, severe, sky-wrathful. Painterly hand-painted look, subtle glowing energy accents, clean shapes readable from an elevated three-quarter camera. Neutral standing pose, legs clear of the body, no base. Clean closed game-ready geometry with separate materials: bronze armor, marble body, lightning glow. No text, logos, rider, gore, or floating fragments.

technical_constraints.origin: center of the four-hoof footprint at ground level
technical_constraints.topology: remesh to a board-piece budget during cleanup; generated face count is expected to be far above budget (AI-050 precedent: 575k-622k tris)

elevenlabs.sfx_brief: SFX GROUP ZEUS_CHARACTER — shared sound family for 10 Zeus Character cards. Palette: crackling electricity, bronze impacts, thunderous lows. Design 5 short game-ready effects sharing one reverb space and material language: select (0.2s), deploy/place (0.8s), attack (0.7s), hit (0.4s), death (1.2s). Cues covered: DAMAGE (effect), DEPLOY (placement thump), DESTROY (destruction crash), MELEE/RANGED (effect), MOVE (movement whoosh). WAV 48kHz/24-bit, peaks -6dB, no music, no voice. File naming: zeus_character_<cue>.wav
elevenlabs.generation_notes: ElevenLabs generates no shorter than 0.5 s, so select (0.2 s) and hit (0.4 s) are generated at 0.5 s and trimmed at integration. The results are group assets, shared by all 10 ZEUS_CHARACTER cards.
muse_brief_flags: The brief's five designed effects (select/deploy/attack/hit/death) do not match its covered cue list: MOVE is covered but has no designed effect, and select has no matching cue. The coordinator should generate a MOVE cue as the fifth effect or ask Muse before running.

source.name: Leviathan Wakeborn
source.description: A massive bioframe rising in the wake of old sea gods.

requests.silhouette_notes: Tall vertical S-curve with the head and crest high and no limbs. Its tall, thin outline contrasts with the low, wide ram and the squat gate.

meshy.prompt: Stylized 3D game miniature for a hex-tile tactics board game: Leviathan Wakeborn, an original Poseidon-faction sea beast. A massive serpentine leviathan rising upright in a tall S-curve from a coiled lower body, finned crest, heavy jaw, dark bronze scale plates overgrown with coral, bioluminescent teal glow along its ridges. Silhouette: tall vertical coil, head and crest high, no limbs. Ancient, crushing, relentless. Painterly hand-painted look, readable from an elevated three-quarter camera. The coils form its own footprint; no water, rocks, or scenic base. Clean closed game-ready geometry with separate materials: scales, coral, glow. No text, logos, gore, tentacle clutter, or floating fragments.

technical_constraints.origin: center of the coil footprint at ground level

source.name: Abyss Gate
source.description: A colossal seal protecting the deepest arcology.

requests.silhouette_notes: Wide, low mass centered on a round sealed door. Reads as architecture, not a creature. It was chosen over Zeus spires because a tall spire would echo the Skyline Seer's upright staff.

meshy.prompt: Stylized 3D game miniature for a hex-tile tactics board game: Abyss Gate, an original Poseidon-faction fortress structure. A colossal circular sealed vault door set in a thick squat arch of dark stone and bronze, flanked by two low buttress towers, coral growth on the masonry, a glowing bioluminescent teal seal ring at the center with leviathan relief motifs. Silhouette: wide, low, heavy ring-in-arch mass that fits one hex tile, flat underside. Ancient, crushing, immovable. Painterly hand-painted look, readable from an elevated three-quarter camera. Clean closed game-ready geometry with separate materials: stone, bronze, coral, glow. No text, logos, characters, water, terrain, or floating fragments.

technical_constraints.topology: remesh to a board-piece budget during cleanup; generated face count is expected to be far above budget (AI-050 precedent: 575k-622k tris)

muse_brief_flags: The brief designs attack/hit/death effects, but the card's cues are only CLICK/DEPLOY/DESTROY. The coordinator should generate only select (CLICK), deploy (DEPLOY), and death (DESTROY), which saves the attack/hit credits, unless Muse confirms otherwise.

credit_policy.meshy_estimate_basis: One Text to 3D Meshy 6 preview generation. AI-050 was charged 20 credits (3,150 -> 3,130) on 2026-09-27. Texture and remesh are extra and need separate approval.
credit_policy.elevenlabs_estimate_basis: No estimate yet. The coordinator records the flow's estimate in tracking.json and gets PO approval before running. The AI-051 precedent is 158.4 credits for a 5-cue x 4-candidate flow.
credit_policy.resubmission: Never resubmit an uncertain paid job. Before submitting, check the provider history for an existing job for this card and record its ID.

review_gates.check: validate_requests.py exits 0 and the unit tests pass
PO approves the exact credit estimate per job. Record the approval in tracking.json.credit_estimate and the queue.
job_id (or history identification), submitted_at, submitted_by, and the balance before/after go into tracking.json. State becomes SUBMITTED.

Silhouette matches silhouette_class from the board camera, the key features are present (ram horns / upright coil / sealed ring door), and there is no existing-IP likeness. Fail means REJECT, not a silent regenerate.

GLB passes the AI-054 check_glb.py checks for scale, origin, up axis, and naming. A remesh to the board budget is produced. The audio is unclipped, nonverbal, and matches the requested durations and group naming.
Unity import succeeds, with an in-game screenshot and a listen in a dense tactical mix. After that the final manifest row and commit are made. Generated does not mean accepted.
